meta.author: Sudan Historian
meta.purpose: Far-end anchors for batch 1 relation arrows (db/group_layers, Map Designer 4539333). Wikidata labels/coords checked live via wikidata.org API on 2026-10-24; entity-place pairing checked in the GHA full texts on the box.
meta.wikidata_note: Coordinates are Wikidata P625 (point), not boundaries. Arabic labels are Wikidata's, a working translation needing native review.
meta.rules: Anchors are APPROXIMATE points only; no limits implied.

verified.quote: al-Mukurra (in Graeco-Coptic, Makuria) with its capital in Dunkula (Old Dongola)

verified.entity: Turco-Egyptian government, its forces, and al-Zubayr
verified.quote: a governor-general based at the newly founded town of Khartoum
verified.caveat: Khartoum is the seat of the regime only after it was founded in the 1820s. For the 1821 Sennar capitulation (rel-funj-05) and the 1822 Shendi revolt (rel-jaaliyyin-03) the anchor is a symbol of the regime, not where its forces stood. Al-Zubayr was a trader active in Bahr al-Ghazal, not based in Khartoum; for rel-fur-06 the anchor stands for the regime only.
verified.badge: APPROXIMATE; EDITORIAL for rel-funj-05, rel-jaaliyyin-03 and rel-fur-06

verified.quote: Until then the Fur sultans had no fixed capital. The growth of a permanent capital at al-Fashir ... in the reign of 'Abd al-Rahman
verified.caveat: Before 'Abd al-Rahman's reign the Fur sultans had no fixed capital, so for earlier relations (rel-fur-01 Sulayman Solongdungu, rel-fur-04 Ya'qub / 'Umar Lel) al-Fashir is an anachronistic symbol of the sultanate.
verified.badge: APPROXIMATE; EDITORIAL for pre-'Abd al-Rahman arrows

verified.label_issue: Wikidata's English label reads 'Sengs' (an error on Wikidata); the Arabic label سنار and description 'Town in Sennar State, Sudan' match. Display 'Sennar'; we do not edit Wikidata.
verified.quote: the two monarchs conducted the war from their capitals ... Iyasu II marched at the head of a large Ethiopian army against Sennar
'Abdallah Djamma' and his descendants, the 'Abdallabi, administered the new regime from Kerri, north of Soba, on the main Nile

new_anchors.quote: the verification of Christian influence at 'Ayn Farah led him [Arkell] to restate it, saying that Tundjur rule was under Nubian protection ... Uri in northern Darfur, in Arkell's view, was a centre of Tundjur rule
new_anchors.note: Uri is the better-attested centre in the text but has no Wikidata item found; Ain Farah is the Wikidata-listed site the same page ties to the Tunjur. Both rest on Arkell's hypotheses as reported by Kropacek.

new_anchors.quote: the legendary Tundjur 'pagan kingdom' of Wadai with its capital at Wara
new_anchors.note: The registered source names Wara as capital of the Tunjur-era Wadai kingdom, not explicitly of the 17th–18th-century sultanate in rel-fur-04. Wikidata Q1132786 (Ouaddai Empire) lists a capital (P36) but I did not use an unsourced claim.

new_anchors.quote: By May 1922, this period of resistance in Dar Masalit had ended.
new_anchors.note: Q56545571 is a geographic region (P31 Q82794) with no labels on Wikidata; the point is its region point, not a town. No Arabic label; Arabic 'دار مساليت' would be our working translation, needing native review.

nulls.reason: GHA5_CH7 p.185 only says the Shaykiyya 'became a major force in the region of Dunkula'; GHA7_CH4 p.74 names no place. No registered source I have read names a Shaigiyya settlement, so no point is given. Dongola is already the Danagla anchor and would be misleading.

GHA5_CH7 p.185: 'Hamadj' was 'applied by Sudanese Arabs to some of the ancient peoples of the Djazira', a region with no point. As regents they ruled at Sennar, so an arrow Funj-Hamaj would have zero length. Gezira State (Q309469) is a modern unit and would be anachronistic.
